1.1: In the third year Jehoiakim was king in Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came through and put Jerusalem under siege.
1.2: God let Jehoiakim get taken, along with some of the sacred stuff from God's temple. Nebuchadnezzar took all that back to Babylon—to Shinar—and dropped it off in his god's treasure house.
1.3: Then the king told his right-hand man, Ashpenaz—the dude in charge of all the eunuchs—to go round up some young Israelites. Not just any kids though—he wanted some from royal blood and noble families.
1.4: They had to be fine, flawless, smart as a whip, quick on the uptake, and polished enough to serve in the king's palace. Basically, top-tier. And they had to be ready to learn Babylon's language and culture.
1.5: The king even set them up with a daily meal plan—his own rich food and wine. They were gon' train for three years, and after that, step into the royal service.
1.6: Outta all the Judah boys, there were four standouts: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
1.7: But of course, they tried to rename them: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abed-Nego.
1.8: But Daniel? He made up his mind—he wasn't gon' get caught up in all that. No king's fancy food, no royal wine. He didn't wanna defile himself. So he asked the chief eunuch if he could opt out.
1.9: Now God had already made the chief eunuch vibe with Daniel, so he liked him.
1.10: But the eunuch was like, "Man, I feel you, but I'm scared. If y'all start lookin' weak and raggedy, the king gon' come for my neck—literally."
1.11: So Daniel slid over to the steward—the dude the eunuch put in charge of him, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—and pitched a plan.
1.12: "Look," he said, "give us just veggies and water for ten days. No meat, no wine. Just test it out."
1.13: "After the ten days, check how we look compared to the others eating that royal menu. Then make your call."
1.14: The steward agreed. Ran the trial for ten days.
1.15: And by the end of it? They looked healthier and fuller than all the others.
1.16: So the steward switched up the program. No more royal food or wine for them—just the veggies they asked for.
1.17: And God came through. Gave all four of them mad wisdom and knowledge. Daniel even got insight into visions and dreams.
1.18: When the three years were up, the king called 'em in. The chief eunuch brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
1.19: The king talked to each of them, but nobody stood out like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They were different. So the king kept them close.
1.20: Anytime the king needed advice, wisdom, or understanding, he went to them. And every time, they were ten times better than the magicians and astrologers in his whole kingdom.
1.21: And Daniel? He stayed serving all the way until King Cyrus pulled up on the throne.

2.1: So in year two of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, bruh started havin' dreams—real wild ones. His spirit was shook, and he couldn't sleep no more.
2.2: So he called up all his magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and Chaldean know-it-alls. He needed somebody to tell him what he dreamed and what it meant.
2.3: He said, "Y'all, I had a dream that got me twisted—I need to know what it was."
2.4: The Chaldeans answered him in Aramaic, "Long live the king! Just tell us what you dreamed, and we'll break it down for you."
2.5: But the king was like, "Nah—I ain't playin'. If y'all can't tell me the dream and what it means, I'm cuttin' y'all to pieces and turning your houses into ash piles."
2.6: "But if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, I'll hook y'all up with gifts, rewards, and big respect. Now tell me what I dreamed and what it means."
2.7: They tried again: "King, just tell us the dream first—we'll handle the interpretation."
2.8: But Nebuchadnezzar was fed up. "I see what y'all tryna do—stallin'. Y'all just buyin' time 'cause y'all know I ain't changin' my mind."
2.9: "If y'all don't tell me the dream, then I already know y'all just gon' lie to me till things blow over. Tell me the dream first—then I'll know y'all ain't just makin' up the meaning."
2.10: The Chaldeans replied, "Ain't no human on earth can do what you ask! No king, no ruler, nobody ever asked something like this before."
2.11: "This thing you ask is too deep. Only the gods could answer that—and they don't live here with us flesh-and-blood folks."
2.12: That sent the king into full rage mode. He ordered all the wise men in Babylon to be executed.
2.13: The decree dropped quick, and they started hunting folks down—including Daniel and his crew.
2.14: But Daniel kept his cool. He hollered at Arioch—the captain of the king's guard—with wisdom and tact.
2.15: "Yo, Arioch, why the king poppin' off like this? What's the rush?"
2.16: After Arioch broke it down, Daniel went and requested some time from the king to figure out the dream and its meaning.
2.17: Then he rushed home and told his boys—Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—what was goin' down.
2.18: He asked them to pray hard and seek mercy from the God of heaven, so they wouldn't die with the rest of Babylon's wise men.
2.19: That night, God showed Daniel the dream in a vision. And Daniel immediately praised the God of heaven.
2.20: Daniel said, "Blessed be God's name forever and ever, He got all the wisdom and the power.
2.21: He flips seasons and kings, Gives wisdom to the wise And knowledge to those that seek Him.
2.22: He reveals deep, hidden things; He sees through the dark, And He shines light right through it.
2.23: Thank You, God of my ancestors, You gave me wisdom and strength. You answered our prayers— Now I know what the king saw!"
2.24: Daniel went straight to Arioch and said, "Don't kill the wise men. Take me to the king—I got what he's lookin' for."
2.25: Arioch rushed Daniel in and said, "King, I found someone from the Judah captives who can break down your dream."
2.26: The king asked Daniel (aka Belteshazzar), "Can you really tell me what I dreamed and what it means?"
2.27: Daniel said, "Look—ain't no magician, astrologer, or psychic on earth who could pull this off."
2.28: "But there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets. He's showin' you, O king, what's gon' happen later on. Here's what you saw:
2.29: "While you were lying in bed, thinkin' 'bout the future, God pulled back the curtain and gave you the preview."
2.30: "And He ain't show me this 'cause I'm smarter than anyone else. It's so we could explain it to you, and you'd understand what's been stirrin' in your heart."
2.31: "You saw a giant statue—huge and shiny. It was wild. Just awe-inspiring."
2.32: "The head was gold, chest and arms were silver, belly and thighs bronze."
2.33: "Its legs were iron, but the feet were a mix—part iron, part clay."
2.34: "Then outta nowhere, a stone—cut out without human hands—came through and smashed the statue at the feet."
2.35: "Everything—the iron, clay, bronze, silver, gold—crumbled like dust in the wind. The wind blew it all away. But that stone? It turned into a mountain and filled the whole earth."
2.36: "That was your dream. Now here's what it means…"
2.37: "You, O king, are a king of kings. God gave you this kingdom, all that power, and glory."
2.38: "He gave you rule over everybody and everything—humans, animals, birds. You're the head of gold."
2.39: "But after you, another kingdom will rise—less glorious. Then a third kingdom, made of bronze, will take over and rule the earth."
2.40: "After that, a fourth one—strong like iron. Iron crushes everything, and that's how this kingdom will be—breaking all that came before it."
2.41: "Now the feet and toes you saw, made of iron and clay? That means the kingdom gon' be divided. Still strong, but unstable."
2.42: "Some parts solid, some fragile. It's mixed like iron and clay—they don't stick together."
2.43: "And that's how this empire will be—trying to unify through alliances and mixing peoples, but it won't hold."
2.44: "But in the middle of all that, God gon' set up His own kingdom. It'll never be destroyed. It won't get handed off to nobody else. It's gon' crush every other kingdom and last forever."
2.45: "Just like that stone you saw smashing everything, that's God telling you what's coming. It's real. It's locked in."
2.46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar hit the floor—face down before Daniel. Had folks bring incense and offerings to honor him.
2.47: He said, "Yo, your God is the real deal—the God of gods, the Lord of kings, the One who actually reveals mysteries."
2.48: Then he put Daniel on! Gave him gifts, made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and head boss over all the wise men.
2.49: And Daniel looked out for his boys too—got Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego promoted over the province while he himself stayed posted at the king's gate.

3.1: So King Nebuchadnezzar got real bold—he built a gold statue 90 feet tall and 9 feet wide. Set it up out in the plain of Dura in Babylon like it was the new hot thing.
3.2: He sent out invites to everybody in charge—governors, judges, treasurers, politicians, counselors, mayors, and all the big shots—to come through for the dedication ceremony of this gold statue he put up.
3.3: And sure enough, all of 'em showed up and stood in front of the golden idol King Neb set up, tryna act impressed.
3.4: Then a loud-voiced hype man stepped up and said, "Listen up! This message for everybody—no matter where you from or what language you speak.
3.5: When you hear the beat drop—horns, flutes, harps, all that—you better bow down and worship this gold statue the king made.
3.6: If you don't? You goin' in the fire. Not tomorrow. Not later. Immediately."
3.7: So the music hit, and all the people—no matter where they from—fell out and worshiped that gold image like sheep.
3.8: But not everybody was with it. Some Chaldeans ran they messy selves to the king and started snitchin'.
3.9: "O king, live forever," they said, all fake respectful.
3.10: "Didn't you make a decree that anybody who hears the music gotta bow down and worship your statue?
3.11: And if they don't, they supposed to get thrown into the fire—like right away?
3.12: Well, sir… these three Hebrew boys—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego—the ones you gave top jobs to in Babylon? Yeah, they not doin' it. They don't care about your gods or your statue."
3.13: Nebuchadnezzar lost it—mad mad. He ordered those three brought to him immediately.
3.14: "Is it true?" he asked them. "Y'all ain't serving my gods or bowin' to my gold image?"
3.15: "Look—I'll give you one more chance. Music bout to play, and if y'all just fall down and worship it, cool. But if not, y'all gettin' tossed in that furnace. And tell me—what god gonna save y'all then?"
3.16: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego kept it 100. "We don't even need to respond to that, King.
3.17: Our God can save us from the fire, and from you too."
3.18: "But even if He don't—we still ain't bowin'. Period."
3.19: That really set Nebuchadnezzar off. He was heated, literally and figuratively. He told 'em to crank the furnace seven times hotter than usual.
3.20: Then he picked the strongest soldiers in his squad to tie them up and toss 'em in.
3.21: They bound up the three men—still wearing their coats, pants, turbans and all—and threw them in.
3.22: The furnace was so hot, it burned up the soldiers just for gettin' close.
3.23: And Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego? They fell into the flames—fully tied up.
3.24: But then Nebuchadnezzar jumped up. "Wait—ain't we throw three men in that fire?"
3.25: "Yes, King, just three." "Well LOOK," the king said. "I see four men walkin' around in the fire—loose—and they ain't hurt. And that fourth one? He look divine—like the Son of God."
3.26: So Nebuchadnezzar went up to the mouth of the furnace and shouted, "Shadrach! Meshach! Abed-Nego! Servants of the Most High God—come out here!" They stepped out the fire like it was nothing.
3.27: All the royal officials came running and saw that the fire ain't do a thing to them—not a hair singed, no clothes burned, not even a whiff of smoke.
3.28: Then the king had to give props: "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego! He sent His angel and saved them because they trusted Him. They defied my command and risked everything to stay loyal to their God."
3.29: "So I'm making a new rule—anybody who talks reckless about their God? Off with them! And their house? Ashes. Ain't no god out here who can rescue like this one."
3.30: And then, like the story couldn't get any better, the king gave them an even higher promotion in Babylon.

4.1: King Nebuchadnezzar sent this out to everybody — all the people, every nation and language across the whole earth: "Peace and blessings to y'all."
4.2: "I gotta let y'all know what the Most High God done did for me — all the signs and miracles He worked out."
4.3: "His signs? Off the chain. His wonders? Powerful. His kingdom last forever, and He always runnin' things — every generation."
4.4: I was chillin' in my palace, feelin' real good.
4.5: Then boom — I had this dream that shook me. I was shook in my sleep, my mind all over the place.
4.6: So I sent out a message to bring in all the wise folk in Babylon so they could break down the dream for me.
4.7: The magicians, astrologers, fortune tellers — all of 'em came. I told 'em the dream, but none of them could tell me what it meant.
4.8: Then Daniel pulled up (y'all know, the one they call Belteshazzar, named after one of my gods — but he got the Spirit of the Holy God in him). I told him the dream too.
4.9: I said, "Belteshazzar, chief over all these magicians — I know you got God's Spirit in you, and no mystery stress you out. Help me out with this vision."
4.10: "Here's what I saw while I was layin' in bed: There was this big tree in the middle of the earth — real tall."
4.11: "It kept growin', got super strong. So tall it touched the sky and everybody on earth could see it."
4.12: "The leaves were beautiful, it had a ton of fruit, and it fed everybody. Wild animals rested under it, birds lived in its branches — everything needed that tree."
4.13: "Then I saw in my dream a 'watcher' — a holy one — come down from heaven."
4.14: "He yelled out loud: 'Cut the tree down! Chop off the branches, strip the leaves, scatter the fruit! Let the animals and birds dip out.'"
4.15: "'But don't touch the stump — leave it in the ground, lock it down with iron and bronze. Let it stay in the grass, and let the dew fall on it. Let him eat grass like the animals.'"
4.16: "'Change his heart from human to animal. Let seven seasons pass over him.'"
4.17: "'This is what the holy ones decided — so everybody will know the Most High run this. He pick who He want to be in charge, even folks y'all wouldn't expect.'"
4.18: "That's what I dreamed. Now, Belteshazzar, break it down for me. The rest of these wise men ain't got it, but I know you do — 'cause the Spirit of the Holy God stay with you."
4.19: Daniel (aka Belteshazzar) stood there quiet, shook for a minute, thinkin' hard. The king said, "Don't let this dream trip you up." Daniel said, "King… I wish this dream was about your enemies and not you."
4.20: "That big tree you saw, growin' tall and strong, reachin' the sky, seen all over the world…"
4.21: "With beautiful leaves, mad fruit, animals chillin' underneath, and birds livin' in the branches…"
4.22: "That's you, King. You done grown strong and powerful. Your greatness touches the heavens, and your rule reach everywhere."
4.23: "But then you saw that holy one come down sayin': 'Chop the tree down, leave the stump, let the dew hit it, let it live like an animal till seven seasons go by.'"
4.24: "That's what's about to happen to you, King. This is what the Most High got planned."
4.25: "You gon' be kicked out from around people. You gon' live like the animals, eat grass like cows. Dew gon' be your shower. This gon' go on for seven seasons — till you realize the Most High is in charge of kings, and He picks who runs things."
4.26: "But the stump stayin' in the ground? That means your kingdom gon' still be yours — once you learn that Heaven is the one who really got the power."
4.27: "So here's my advice, King: do right. Cut out the sin. Show love to the poor. Maybe then your peace will last a little longer."
4.28: And yeah — all this came true for King Nebuchadnezzar.
4.29: A whole year later, he was strollin' around his palace in Babylon, feelin' himself.
4.30: He said, "Ain't this the fly kingdom I built with my own power? All this is mine — for my glory and fame."
4.31: While the words was still comin' out his mouth — BOOM — a voice came down from heaven sayin', "Yo, Nebuchadnezzar! Your kingdom gone!"
4.32: "You ain't gon' be around people no more. You bout to be out here with the animals, eatin' grass. This gon' last seven seasons till you get it through your head: the Most High runs everything."
4.33: That same hour it happened. He got kicked out, ate grass like an ox, his body stayed wet from the dew, hair got long like eagle feathers, nails like bird claws.
4.34: But after that time passed, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven — and my mind came back. I praised the Most High, honored the One who lives forever. His kingdom? Eternal. His rule? Ain't nobody takin' that from Him.
4.35: Everybody on earth? Ain't nothin' compared to Him. He do what He want, both in heaven and down here. Ain't nobody stoppin' Him or questionin' His moves.
4.36: My mind came back, and so did my kingdom — and even more honor than before. My people came back to me, and I got my throne again, plus extra glory.
4.37: So now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, lift up, and honor the King of heaven. Everything He do is right. All His ways are just. And He know how to bring down anybody who's too proud.

5.1: King Belshazzar threw a huge turn-up for a thousand of his people, drinkin' wine right in front of all of 'em.
5.2: While he was sippin', Belshazzar told 'em to go grab them gold and silver cups his daddy Nebuchadnezzar stole from God's temple in Jerusalem, so him, his boys, his wives, and his side chicks could drink outta 'em.
5.3: So they brought them sacred cups from God's temple in Jerusalem, and the king, his folks, his wives, and his side pieces all drank outta 'em.
5.4: They was sippin' wine, hypin' up fake gods made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
5.5: Right then, a hand popped up outta nowhere. Just the fingers. And it started writin' on the wall, near the lamp, in the king's palace. The king saw that hand movin' and writin'.
5.6: His whole face switched up—he was shook. His thoughts had him spiralin', hips got weak, and his knees was knockin' together like drums.
5.7: He screamed for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and fortune-tellers to come through. Then he said, "Whoever can read this mess on the wall and tell me what it mean, I'ma hook you up with purple clothes, gold chain, and make you third in charge around here."
5.8: All them "wise men" showed up, but none of 'em could read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
5.9: That made Belshazzar panic even more—his face got ghostly pale, and his squad didn't know what to say.
5.10: The queen heard what was goin' down and pulled up to the party. She said, "Long live the king! Chill, don't let this mess rattle you or mess up your face.
5.11: There's a dude in your kingdom who got God's Spirit in him. Back in your daddy's day, he was known for bein' full of light, deep wisdom, and understanding—like the gods themselves. King Nebuchadnezzar, your daddy, made him the head over all the magicians, astrologers, and wise folks.
5.12: This man, Daniel—aka Belteshazzar—he got that excellent vibe, knowledge, skill for readin' dreams, crackin' riddles, and explainin' wild stuff. Call Daniel in, and he'll break it down for you."
5.13: So they brought Daniel in front of the king. The king asked, "You that Daniel, one of them exiles from Judah that my daddy brought here?
5.14: I done heard about you—how you got God's Spirit in you, and how you got light, wisdom, and deep understanding.
5.15: My crew—the wise men and astrologers—they couldn't break this thing down for me.
5.16: But I heard you the one who can interpret and explain deep mysteries. If you can read this writing and tell me what it mean, I'ma give you a purple robe, a gold chain, and make you third in charge."
5.17: Daniel said, "You can keep them gifts, or give 'em to somebody else. But I'll still read what's on the wall and tell you what it mean.
5.18: Look king, the Most High God gave your daddy Nebuchadnezzar all his power, status, honor, and shine.
5.19: And 'cause of that, all the folks from every nation and language was scared of him. He killed who he wanted, let live who he wanted, raised up who he wanted, and brought down who he wanted.
5.20: But when he got too full of himself, all prideful and arrogant, God snatched the throne from him and stripped him of all that glory.
5.21: He got kicked out like a wild animal. He lost his mind, lived with donkeys, ate grass like oxen, and stayed drenched in dew 'til he learned that the Most High God runs the kingdom game and puts who He wants on the throne.
5.22: But you, Belshazzar—you knew all this, and still didn't humble yourself.
5.23: Matter fact, you went against the Lord of heaven. You had the nerve to drink wine outta His temple cups, you and your crew, your wives, and your side chicks. Y'all gave props to gods made outta silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone—gods that can't see, hear, or think. But the real God, the one holdin' your breath and controllin' your path? You ain't even acknowledge Him.
5.24: That's why He sent that hand to write what you saw.
5.25: Here's what it said: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
5.26: MENE mean: God done numbered your days as king—it's a wrap.
5.27: TEKEL mean: You been weighed on God's scales, and you came up short.
5.28: PERES mean: Your kingdom's gettin' split up and handed to the Medes and Persians."
5.29: Then Belshazzar kept his word—he gave Daniel the purple fit, put a gold chain on him, and announced that Daniel was now third in command.
5.30: That same night, Belshazzar, king of Babylon, got killed.
5.31: And Darius the Mede came in and took over the kingdom. Dude was 62 years old.

6.1: King Darius thought it was a good idea to put 120 officials over the whole kingdom.
6.2: Over them, he picked three top bosses—Daniel was one of 'em—to make sure them officials ain't mess up or steal so the king ain't lose nothin'.
6.3: Daniel stood out from the rest, 'cause he had that favor on him—an excellent spirit. The king was even thinkin' 'bout puttin' him in charge of the whole thing.
6.4: So the other bosses and officials tried to dig up some dirt on Daniel, tryin' to catch him slippin' in his job. But he was solid—faithful, no mistakes, no funny business.
6.5: They said, "Ain't no way we gon' catch him doin' wrong unless it's got somethin' to do with how he serves his God."
6.6: So all them officials and bosses pulled up on the king and said, "O King Darius, long live the king!
6.7: Look, everybody on your team—bosses, counselors, and all—agree that we should make a new law: for 30 days, nobody can pray to no god or person except you. If they do, throw 'em in the lion's den.
6.8: Go ahead and write it down, king, and seal it—'cause the law of the Medes and Persians can't be changed."
6.9: So King Darius signed off on the law, just like that.
6.10: When Daniel heard the law was signed, he went home. He went upstairs, windows open toward Jerusalem, dropped to his knees three times a day like he always did, and prayed and thanked God.
6.11: Them haters was watchin'—they caught Daniel prayin' and askin' God for help.
6.12: They ran back to the king and said, "Didn't you sign a law sayin' for 30 days nobody can pray to anybody but you, or else they get tossed to the lions?" The king said, "Yeah, that's right. Law of the Medes and Persians. No changes."
6.13: They said, "Well, that dude Daniel—the one you brought from Judah? He don't care nothin' 'bout you or your law. He still prayin' three times a day."
6.14: When the king heard that, he was sick about it. He liked Daniel and spent the whole day tryna figure out a way to save him.
6.15: But the crew came back and pressed him: "You know the law, king. Once you make it, it can't be changed."
6.16: So the king gave in. He told 'em to grab Daniel and throw him in the lions' den. But he told Daniel, "The God you always serve—He gon' rescue you."
6.17: They rolled a big stone over the entrance and the king sealed it with his ring—and with his officials' rings too—so nobody could undo it.
6.18: That night, the king went home but didn't eat, didn't listen to no music, and couldn't even sleep.
6.19: Real early the next morning, he rushed out to the lions' den.
6.20: When he got close, he cried out, hurt and worried. "Daniel! Servant of the living God! Did your God—the one you always serve—save you from the lions?"
6.22: My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They ain't touch me, 'cause I was innocent in His eyes. And I ain't do nothin' wrong to you, either."
6.23: The king was hype. He told them to pull Daniel up out the pit. And Daniel ain't have a scratch on him—'cause he had real faith in his God.
6.24: Then the king ordered the men who tried to snitch on Daniel to be thrown in the lions' den—along with their kids and wives. Before they could even hit the ground, the lions tore 'em up, broke all they bones.
6.25: Then King Darius wrote this letter: "To everybody in the world—every people, nation, and language: Peace to y'all.
6.26: I'm makin' a new rule: In every part of my kingdom, everybody need to show mad respect and fear for the God of Daniel. He the livin' God, He steady and don't switch up. His kingdom ain't goin' nowhere, And He run things forever.
6.27: He saves and rescues, He show out with miracles in heaven and earth. He the One who saved Daniel from them lions."
6.28: So Daniel stayed blessed and kept on thrivin' through the rest of Darius' reign and even when Cyrus the Persian took over.

7.1: In the first year of King Belshazzar's reign in Babylon, Daniel had this wild dream while he was sleepin'. He woke up, wrote it down, and made sure to keep the main points.
7.2: Daniel said, "In my dream that night, I saw the four winds from heaven stirrin' up the big sea.
7.3: Then four crazy lookin' beasts rose up out the sea. Each one looked different from the last.
7.4: The first one looked like a lion but had eagle wings. As I watched, the wings got snatched off. Then it stood up on two feet like a man, and it was given a man's heart.
7.5: Then came the second beast, lookin' like a big ol' bear. It was leaned up on one side, and had three ribs in its mouth like it just finished eatin'. Folks told it, 'Get up and eat even more flesh!'
7.6: After that, I saw a third beast that looked like a leopard. It had four bird wings on its back and four heads. Dominion—like rulership—was given to it.
7.7: Then I saw a fourth beast in another vision that night. Man, this one was terrifying—looked wild and strong, had iron teeth, and was crushin', smashin', and stompin' on whatever was left. It didn't look like nothin' that came before it. It had ten horns.
7.8: While I was thinkin' about them horns, another little horn came up in the middle of 'em, and three of the original horns got snatched out to make room. This new horn had eyes like a man and a mouth that stayed talkin' big talk.
7.9: I watched till thrones got set up, And the Ancient of Days sat down. His fit was white like snow, Hair like pure wool. His throne was straight flames, With wheels burnin' fire.
7.10: A river of fire flowed out from Him. Thousands upon thousands served Him. Millions stood in front of Him. Court was in session, And the books got opened.
7.11: I kept watchin' 'cause that loud-mouth horn was still talkin' wild. Then the beast got killed, and its body got tossed in the fire.
7.12: The other beasts had their power taken too, but they got to live a lil' longer for a set time.
7.13: Then I saw in my dream at night, One like the Son of Man ridin' on the clouds. He came up to the Ancient of Days, And they brought Him near.
7.14: He was handed full dominion, glory, and a kingdom, So that everybody—people from every nation and language—would serve Him. His kingdom gon' last forever, Never gonna pass away or get destroyed.
7.15: Daniel said, "I was torn up on the inside—my spirit was shook. That dream had me messed up.
7.16: So I went up to one of them standin' there and asked what all this meant. He broke it down for me.
7.17: He said, 'Them four beasts? That's four kings gon' rise up from the earth.
7.18: But the people of the Most High—His real ones—gon' get the kingdom and hold it down forever. Ain't nobody takin' it back.'
7.19: But I had to know more 'bout that fourth beast— The one that ain't look like the rest, So mean and powerful, With iron teeth and bronze claws, That devoured, crushed, and stomped everything.
7.20: I needed answers about them ten horns on its head And the one little horn that came up and knocked three down. That little horn had eyes, a loud mouth, and was lookin' real bold.
7.21: I saw that horn makin' war with God's people— And it was actually winnin' for a minute.
7.22: But then the Ancient of Days stepped in, Judged in favor of the saints, And it was finally time for God's people to take over.
7.23: Here's what he said: 'That fourth beast? It's a fourth kingdom that gon' rise up on the earth. It ain't like none before it. It's gon' eat up the whole world, Smash and crush everything in its way.
7.24: The ten horns? That's ten kings from that kingdom. Then another king gon' come after them— He gon' be different, And take down three kings.
7.25: He gon' run his mouth against the Most High, Oppress God's people, And try to change the times and the laws. God's people gon' be under his hand For a time, times, and half a time.
7.26: But then court gon' sit, And they gon' strip his power And destroy him for good.
7.27: After that, the whole kingdom, the power, Everything under heaven Gon' belong to the saints—God's people. His kingdom lasts forever, And every ruler gon' bow down and obey Him.'
7.28: That's where the vision ended. But me? I was real disturbed— My face went pale, And I kept the whole thing to myself.

8.1: In the third year of King Belshazzar's rule, I—Daniel—had another vision. This one came after the first dream I had.
8.2: In the vision, I saw myself in Shushan, the fortress city in the province of Elam. I was standin' by the Ulai River.
8.3: I looked up and saw a ram standin' by the river. It had two horns, both tall, but one was taller than the other—and the taller one came up last.
8.4: The ram was pushin' west, north, and south. Ain't no beast could stand against him. Nobody could rescue from his grip. He did whatever he wanted and got real powerful with it.
8.5: While I was still tryin' to figure it out, a male goat came outta the west, movin' across the whole earth like it was flyin', not even touchin' the ground. It had one big horn between its eyes.
8.6: It ran straight at that ram with the two horns I saw earlier—comin' full speed with serious power.
8.7: It went at the ram with rage, broke both its horns, and the ram ain't have no strength to fight back. The goat slammed him to the ground and stomped him out. Nobody could save the ram.
8.8: The goat got real powerful after that, but right when it was at its peak, the big horn broke off. Then four new horns popped up where that one was, pointin' in all directions.
8.9: Outta one of them four horns, a small horn came up. It started growin' real big toward the south, the east, and even toward the Beautiful Land.
8.10: This little horn got bold—like reachin' up to heaven. It threw down some of the heavenly hosts and some stars and stomped on 'em.
8.11: It even had the nerve to try and act higher than the Prince of the army of heaven. It shut down the daily sacrifices and messed up the temple spot.
8.12: Because folks was wildin' in sin, God let this horn take control, stop the daily offerings, and drag the truth through the mud. And it was successful at it—for a minute.
8.13: Then I heard one holy one talkin', and another one asked, "How long is this mess gonna go on? The daily sacrifices bein' stopped, the holy place and the people gettin' stomped on?"
8.14: The answer came back: "2,300 evenings and mornings. After that, the sanctuary gon' get cleaned up."
8.15: After I saw all this, I was tryna figure out what it meant. Then outta nowhere, someone lookin' like a man showed up.
8.16: I heard a voice callin' from between the Ulai River banks, "Gabriel, break this down for him. Help him understand."
8.17: Gabriel came toward me, and I got so scared I fell face-first to the ground. But he said, "Chill, son of man. This vision is talkin' about the end times."
8.18: While he was speakin', I blacked out—face in the dirt. But he touched me and helped me stand up.
8.19: He said, "I'ma tell you what's gonna go down at the end of all this chaos. It's gonna happen at the time God already set.
8.20: That ram you saw with the two horns? That's the kings of Media and Persia.
8.21: The goat? That's Greece. The big horn between its eyes? That's the first king.
8.22: That horn got broken, and four others rose up in its place. That means four kingdoms will rise from the same empire, but none of them will have the same kind of power.
8.23: Later on, when sin hits its peak, A bold, slick king gon' show up.
8.24: He gon' be powerful—but it won't be his own strength. He gon' cause destruction, He gon' succeed, And he gon' take down the strong and even God's chosen ones.
8.25: He gon' be all about deception, Think he all that in his own heart, Mess up a whole lot of folks while they chillin'. He gon' even try to step to the Prince of princes— But he gon' get taken down, and it won't be by no human hands.
8.26: What you saw in the vision—the one about evenings and mornings—it's true. But lock it down. This for the future, a long time from now."
8.27: I, Daniel, passed out after all that. I was sick for days. But I eventually got up and went back to work for the king. Still, I couldn't stop thinkin' about the vision. I ain't tell nobody, 'cause they wouldn't get it.

9.1: In the first year of Darius—son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by blood—when he got made king over the Babylonian territory,
9.2: I, Daniel, was readin' the scriptures and realized from the prophet Jeremiah that God had said Jerusalem was gon' be desolate for seventy years.
9.3: So I turned my attention to God—prayin', cryin' out, fastin', wearin' sackcloth, and sittin' in ashes.
9.4: I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed, sayin', "Lord, You great and awesome! You keep Your promises and show mercy to the ones who love You and follow Your commandments.
9.5: But we messed up bad—we sinned, acted foul, did what we wanted, rebelled, and straight-up ignored Your instructions and judgments.
9.6: We ain't listen to Your prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our leaders, our parents, and everybody else in the land.
9.7: Lord, You always right, but us? We ashamed—everybody: Judah, Jerusalem, all Israel, whether they close or scattered all over the place. We all in this mess 'cause we turned our back on You.
9.8: We ashamed, Lord—our kings, leaders, and ancestors—'cause we sinned against You.
9.9: But You, Lord our God, got mercy and forgiveness, even when we rebelled.
9.10: We didn't obey Your voice or walk in Your ways like You told us through the prophets.
9.11: All of Israel turned away from Your law and refused to listen. That's why we under the curse You warned us about in the Law of Moses—'cause we sinned against You.
9.12: You kept Your word and brought disaster on us and on our leaders. What happened to Jerusalem? Ain't nobody ever seen destruction like that.
9.13: Just like Moses wrote, all this disaster came down on us—but we still ain't turn to You, Lord, or tried to understand what's real.
9.14: So You let it happen, 'cause You always do what's right—even when we don't listen.
9.15: And now, Lord our God—You the one who brought Your people outta Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for Yourself that still stands—we done messed up and acted wicked.
9.16: Lord, please, based on Your righteousness, turn Your anger away from Jerusalem, Your holy mountain. Our sins and the sins of our ancestors made us and Your city look bad to the nations around us.
9.17: So now, our God, hear Your servant prayin' and cryin' out. For Your sake, shine Your face on Your ruined sanctuary.
9.18: Lord, open Your ears and eyes—see what we goin' through. We ain't bring our prayers to You 'cause we earned anything, but 'cause You got mad mercy.
9.19: Lord, please hear us! Please forgive! Please act! Don't wait no more—for Your own name's sake—'cause this city and Your people belong to You!"
9.20: While I was still prayin'—confessin' my sins and my people's sins, and askin' God to show mercy on His holy mountain—
9.21: While I was still talkin', Gabriel—the same one I seen in the last vision—came flyin' up to me right around the evening sacrifice time.
9.22: He came and said, "Daniel, I'm here to help you understand what's really goin' on.
9.23: As soon as you started prayin', the word went out—and I'm here 'cause you highly favored. So listen close and try to get this vision."
9.24: "God already marked out seventy weeks for your people and your holy city:– To shut down sin,– To put an end to guilt,– To make things right with God,– To bring in everlasting righteousness,– To lock up vision and prophecy,– And to anoint the Most Holy One.
9.25: So know this and understand: From the moment the order goes out to rebuild Jerusalem until the Prince—the Messiah—comes, it'll be seven weeks and sixty-two more weeks. The streets and walls will be rebuilt, even while times stay rough.
9.26: After those sixty-two weeks, the Messiah gon' be cut off—and not for Himself. Then a ruler will come with his people and destroy the city and the temple. It's gon' end like a flood—war and destruction already set to come.
9.27: That ruler gon' confirm a deal with many for one week. But halfway through, he gon' stop the sacrifices and offerings. He gon' do some foul stuff, real disrespectful—set up something nasty and desolate—until God brings the final judgment down on him."

10.1: In the third year of King Cyrus of Persia, I—Daniel, who they also call Belteshazzar—got a vision. The message was real, and it was about some stuff that was gon' take a long time to go down. But I understood it.
10.2: At that time, I had been in deep mourning for three straight weeks.
10.3: I wasn't eatin' no good food—no meat, no wine, not even lotion on my skin—nothin' pleasant touched me the whole time.
10.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was chillin' by the Tigris River.
10.5: I looked up and saw a man—dressed in linen with a gold belt from Uphaz around his waist.
10.6: His body looked like a gemstone, his face was flashin' like lightning, his eyes were like fire, arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice? Sounded like a whole crowd talkin' at once.
10.7: I was the only one who actually saw the vision. The people with me couldn't see it, but they got hit with a wave of fear and dipped out real quick to hide.
10.8: So I was left alone, seein' this heavy vision. My strength vanished, my face went pale, and I had nothin' left in me.
10.9: I heard him talkin' though, and the sound of his voice knocked me straight out—I fell face-first to the ground in a deep sleep.
10.10: Then outta nowhere, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and hands.
10.11: He said, "Daniel, you're deeply loved. Pay attention to what I'm sayin' and stand up—I was sent here for you." And while he talked, I stood up, still shakin'.
10.12: He said, "Don't be scared, Daniel. From the very first day you set your heart to understand and humbled yourself before God, He heard you. That's why I'm here.
10.13: But I got held up—the spiritual prince over Persia blocked me for 21 days. Then Michael, one of the top warriors of heaven, came to help me, 'cause I was stuck fightin' with the kings of Persia.
10.14: Now I'm here to break it down for you—what's gonna happen to your people later on. This vision is about the future."
10.15: While he was talkin', I couldn't even look up—I was speechless, starin' at the ground.
10.16: Then someone who looked human touched my lips. I finally spoke and said, "My lord, this vision got me overwhelmed—I got no strength left.
10.17: How can I even talk to you right now? I'm weak, breathin' heavy, barely holdin' on."
10.18: Then the one who looked like a man touched me again—and I felt stronger.
10.19: He said, "Don't trip, you deeply loved. Peace to you. Be strong, real strong!" As he talked, strength came back to me. I said, "Go ahead and speak—I'm good now. You gave me strength."
10.20: He said, "You know why I came, right? Now I gotta go back and fight that prince of Persia. And after that, the prince of Greece gon' show up.
10.21: But I'ma tell you what's written in the Book of Truth. Ain't nobody ridin' with me in this fight except Michael—your heavenly protector."

11.1: Back in the first year of Darius the Mede, I—yeah, me—stood up to back him up and give him strength.
11.2: Now listen up, I'ma tell you straight: Three more kings gon' rise in Persia, and then a fourth one—way richer than all of them—gon' use his wealth and power to stir up everybody against Greece.
11.3: Then a powerful king gon' pop up, takin' over everything, doin' whatever he wanna do.
11.4: But right when he get strong, his kingdom gon' get broken up and spread out in four directions. It won't go to his kids, and it won't be as strong as before. It's gon' get taken and given to others.
11.5: The king of the South gon' get strong, and one of his boys gon' get even stronger and end up runnin' the show with a heavy hand.
11.6: After some time, they'll try to link up—one of the Southern king's daughters gon' marry the Northern king to keep the peace. But it won't last. She gon' lose power, he gon' fall too, and the whole setup gon' collapse, includin' the people who tried to hold it all together.
11.7: But one of her folks gon' rise up and come with an army. He gon' storm the North, tear it up, and take the W.
11.8: He'll snatch their gods, gold, silver, and valuables, and haul it all back to Egypt. He gon' outlive the Northern king, too.
11.9: Eventually the king of the North gon' try to come back at the South, but he gon' end up retreatin' to his own turf.
11.10: But his sons ain't gon' let it slide. They gon' raise a massive army and charge through, makin' moves. Then one of 'em gon' come back to his stronghold and stir things up.
11.11: The king of the South gon' get heated and go to war against him. The Northern king gon' pull up with a huge army, but the South gon' beat him and wipe out a whole bunch of his folks.
11.12: But after that, the Southern king gon' get cocky and think he up, but it won't last—he won't be able to hold on to it.
11.13: 'Cause the Northern king gon' come back with an even bigger army and better gear, and after a few years, he gon' be back on the attack.
11.14: During all this chaos, some folks—including violent ones from your own people—gon' rise up against the South, thinkin' they fulfillin' prophecy. But they gon' get dropped.
11.15: The king of the North gon' come through, build siege ramps, and take a fortified city. The South's troops won't be able to hold him back—not even their best soldiers.
11.16: Whoever comes at him, he'll do whatever he want. Nobody can stop him. He even gon' take over the Beautiful Land (that's Israel), and bring serious destruction with him.
11.17: He gon' try to lock in full control of the kingdom by sendin' in his daughter—thinkin' she gon' help him win. But she won't be loyal, and the plan gon' flop.
11.18: Then he gon' set his sights on the coastlands and take over a bunch of them. But some leader gon' push back and embarrass him, and he gon' fall back.
11.19: After that, he'll try to focus on home base, but he gon' trip, fall, and disappear—nobody'll be able to save him.
11.20: Somebody else gon' take his place and raise taxes across the land. But he won't last long—he'll be taken out quietly, not even in battle.
11.21: After him, a shady dude gon' sneak in—he ain't even royalty like that. He gon' come in smooth, take over with manipulation and schemes.
11.22: Folks gon' fall like a flood before him—including the "prince of the covenant."
11.23: After makin' fake alliances, he gon' turn sneaky and rise up with just a small crew.
11.24: He gon' roll up on rich spots like it's nothin', doin' stuff his ancestors never did—spreading out the loot to win people over, settin' traps against strongholds. But it won't last forever.
11.25: Then he gon' get bold and go at the king of the South with a huge army. The South gon' respond with a mighty army too, but he gon' get betrayed.
11.26: His own people—the ones eatin' at his table—gon' set him up. His army gon' get wiped, and many gon' die.
11.27: Both kings gon' be sittin' at the same table, straight lyin' to each other, schemin', but none of it gon' work out, 'cause God already set the end time.
11.28: On his way home, the Northern king gon' be mad at God's covenant people, stir up drama, then head back to his land.
11.29: At the set time, he gon' come back at the South, but it won't go like it did before.
11.30: Ships from Cyprus gon' push back on him. He gon' take it personal, rage out on God's people, and cause even more damage.
11.31: He'll send troops to mess up the temple, stop the daily offerings, and set up the "abomination of desolation."
11.32: He'll use slick talk to corrupt folks who already wildin'. But the real ones—those who know their God—gon' stay strong and do big things.
11.33: Wise folks gon' teach others, even though they gon' be hunted, burned, locked up, and robbed for a while.
11.34: When they fall, they'll get a little help—but some fake folks gon' join the movement for clout.
11.35: Even some of the wise gon' fall so they can be refined and purified, 'cause the final time ain't here yet—it's still on God's schedule.
11.36: Then this king gon' do whatever he want. He gon' boost himself above every god and talk crazy against the God of gods. He gon' prosper until God's wrath finishes up, 'cause what God say is gon' happen.
11.37: He won't care 'bout the gods of his ancestors, won't be interested in women, won't respect any god—he think he above all that.
11.38: But instead, he gon' worship war and power, honor a foreign god nobody ever heard of, and throw money and treasures at it.
11.39: He gon' push that god's agenda, give certain folks power, and divide land for a check.
11.40: At the end time, the king of the South gon' pull up on him—but the king of the North gon' come like a hurricane, with chariots, horses, and a whole navy. He gon' blow through countries.
11.41: He'll hit the Glorious Land (Israel), and take down a bunch of nations. But Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites gon' escape.
11.42: He gon' take over all kinds of lands—even Egypt won't be safe.
11.43: He gon' control all Egypt's money and treasures. Libya and Ethiopia gon' be right behind him.
11.44: But then he gon' get shook by news from the east and north. He gon' go out wildin', ready to destroy and kill.
11.45: He'll pitch his royal tents between the sea and God's holy mountain—but that's where his run ends. Nobody gon' help him.

12.1: Around that time, Michael—the big angel who watches over your people—gon' step in. It's gon' be a time of trouble like the world ain't never seen before. But your people—the ones whose names in the Book—they gon' be saved.
12.2: A whole bunch of folks who been sleepin' in the dirt gon' wake up— Some to eternal life, Others to shame and eternal disgrace.
12.3: The wise ones gon' shine bright, Like the stars up in the sky. And the ones who helped folks get right with God? They gon' shine forever too.
12.4: But you, Daniel? Close up this vision. Seal the book 'til the end times. Folks gon' be runnin' all over, And knowledge gon' be on a whole new level.
12.5: Then I looked up and saw two more people—one standin' on each side of the river.
12.6: One of them asked the man dressed in linen who was floatin' above the water, "How long 'til all this stuff goes down?"
12.7: I heard the man in linen raise both hands to heaven and swear by the One who lives forever, "It's gon' last a time, times, and half a time. When God's people look completely broken, That's when all this gon' finally wrap up."
12.8: I heard it, but I ain't really get it. So I asked, "Sir, how's all this gon' end?"
12.9: He said, "Go 'head, Daniel. The words are locked down 'til the end time.
12.10: A lotta folks gon' get purified, cleaned up, and made right. But the wicked? They gon' keep wildin'. They won't get it—but the wise will understand."
12.11: "From the day the daily sacrifices get stopped And that nasty abomination gets put in place, You count 1,290 days.
12.12: But blessed is the one who waits it out and makes it to day 1,335.
12.13: And you, Daniel—go on and rest. You gon' rise up and get your reward at the very end."
